recommendation: Keep the source-changing commit as-is. Further work would only be needed if CBCC wants a normative rule for exact break-glass/disaster codes or wants to narrow the example to a specific Consent.provision.action code, which is outside this applied example request.
issue_request: FHIR-13420 was Published / Persuasive for Consent. It asked for an example showing a privacy consent that forbids both normal treatment sharing and emergency break-glass use, with no Consent structure or codelist changes required, and with a comment noting that other codes such as BTG and disaster-related purposes might be needed.
initial_application: No local source commit explicitly mentioned FHIR-13420. Git history shows b6c8eb172f added source/consent/consent-example-No-Emergency.xml in January 2019, later Consent model work updated it to the current decision/provision pattern, and c69d71aa21 created the active Consent examples list without this example. The remaining gaps were example-list registration and the requested BTG/disaster-code comment.
additional_context: Consent is active in source/fhir.ini. FHIR-39597 later moved Consent.provision.type to Consent.decision and made provision levels alternate from the base decision, so the current example's permit base plus first-level TREAT/ETREAT provision is the current-model equivalent of denying those matching purposes. FHIR-13419 was only an Organization/HIE example request and was resolved no-change; community searches found no conflicting Zulip or Confluence evidence.
reconciliation: Edited source/consent/list-Consent-examples.xml to reference Consent/consent-example-No-Emergency and edited source/consent/consent-example-No-Emergency.xml to add the requested comment about BTG and disaster-related purpose codes. No structural, binding, or terminology changes were made.
source_changes: source/consent/consent-example-No-Emergency.xml: added an XML comment noting that policies may also need BTG or disaster-related purpose codes.
source/consent/list-Consent-examples.xml: registered Consent/consent-example-No-Emergency in the active Consent examples list.
